title: Modules courbes elliptiques en caractéristiques ≠2 : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from §2 'Courbes relatives de type (0,4)'): S is a base scheme with 2 invertible. X/S is a P^1-bundle and I ⊂ X is a relative divisor, finite étale of degree 4. Aut_S(I) is locally isomorphic to S_4 and contains a canonical normal subgroup V_I, locally isomorphic to (Z/2)^2. I is a V_I-torsor, and by the Proposition on p.53 the action of V_I on I extends uniquely to an action on X.

This page completes the dictionary describing the moduli of (X, I) step by step.

(i) Octahedral structure and the section. A faithful action of a Klein four-group V on a P^1-bundle is the same as an 'octahedral structure'. Each nontrivial involution of V has 2 fixed points, so there are 6 fixed points in all, forming the vertices of an octahedron. Call this degree-6 divisor Δ; the normalizer of V in PGL_2 is the octahedral group S_4. Given such an action, I is a free V-orbit in X∖Δ, so I is the same as a section of (X∖Δ)/V. Conversely, a section of (X∖Δ)/V gives back I as its inverse image in X∖Δ. The first lines of the page finish this argument.

(ii) Rigid part. The data of V on S (étale group scheme locally (Z/2)^2) is equivalent to the degree-3 étale cover J of its nontrivial elements, roughly J ≅ V^*∖0. That in turn is equivalent to a projective line bundle Σ = Σ_J over S together with a relative divisor D_J ≅ J of degree 3.
- Concretely (next page), Σ_J is the line {Σ_{i∈J} y_i = 0} and D_J = {y_i = 0}, i.e. Σ_J = X/V with D_J the branch divisor.
- Σ*_J = Σ_J∖D_J is a twisted form of P^1∖{0,1,∞} = M_{0,4}.

(iii) Twisting datum. b) A V-torsor K over S is equivalent to a principal V-covering X* → Σ*_J whose class in H^0(S, H^1(Σ*_J/S, V)) is the canonical one. Here H^1(Σ*_J/S, V) ≅ Hom(V_J, V), because the mod-2 abelianized fundamental group of the line minus three points is (Z/2)^J/diag = V_J. The canonical element is the identity V_J → V = V_J.
- The correspondence is X* = K ∧^V Σ*_{J,2}.
- Σ*_{J,2} is the 'universal' principal V_J-covering. On the next page it is the conic Σ x_i^2 = 0, with V_J ≅ F_2^J/F_2 acting by sign changes and the quotient map x_i ↦ x_i^2 = y_i (a Kummer/Fermat-type cover branched over D_J).
- The marginal NB says that this covering realizes the local (relative to S) mod-2 abelianized π_1 of Σ*_J/S, with the identity map on V_J.

(iv) Outcome (completed on p.55). (X, I) ↔ (J, K, x), where x is a section of Σ*_J, namely the image of I in X/V. When I is constant (I_S), J and Σ_J are fixed, and the data reduce to the section x of Σ*_J (the 'λ-parameter') together with the torsor K.

This is the relative, base-independent form of the classical picture: P^1 with 4 points, quotient by the Klein group of double transpositions, λ-line minus 3 points, Fermat conic as Klein cover. It serves the study of the moduli of elliptic curves in characteristic ≠ 2 via the double cover of X branched along I, whose 2-torsion is V. It is the relative version of the M_{0,4} ↔ M_{1,1}(2) dictionary.
errors: No mathematical error is visible. Small gap: the identification H^0(S, H^1(Σ*_J/S, V)) ≅ Hom(V_J, V) uses that 2 is invertible on S (μ_2 = Z/2) and needs a relative/étale base-change argument. The text only asserts it.

Existence of X* with the prescribed class needs the vanishing of the obstruction in H^2(S, V) from the Leray sequence. This is supplied implicitly by the global universal covering Σ*_{J,2}; Grothendieck does not spell it out on this page.
The bijection between principal V-coverings with the given monodromy class and V-torsors on S (via K ∧^V Σ*_{J,2}) holds because the class is fixed. The automorphisms are tacitly taken into account.

ideas.what: Faithful Klein-four action on a P^1-bundle is equivalent to an 'octahedral structure' (the 6 fixed points). A degree-4 étale divisor is a V-orbit, i.e. a section of (X∖Δ)/V.
ideas.modern_name: Klein four-subgroup of PGL_2, octahedral normalizer, twisted forms of P^1 with group action

ideas.what: Klein four-group scheme V over S ↔ degree-3 étale cover J ↔ P^1-bundle Σ_J with étale degree-3 divisor D_J
ideas.modern_name: S_3-torsors / cubic étale algebras and twisted forms of (P^1, {0,1,∞})

ideas.what: Universal principal V_J-covering of Σ*_J given by the conic Σx_i^2=0 → line Σy_i=0. H^1(Σ*_J/S, V) ≅ Hom(V_J, V), and X* = K ∧^V Σ*_{J,2}.
ideas.modern_name: Kummer/Fermat cover of P^1∖{0,1,∞} realizing π_1^ab⊗Z/2; level-2 structure; twisting by torsors
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (Legendre/λ-function, Fermat curves); relative formulation folklore
ideas.where_published: Theme of M_{0,4}, M_{1,1} and P^1 minus 3 points appears in Esquisse d'un programme, but not this explicit construction

ideas.what: Moduli of (P^1-bundle, étale degree-4 divisor) as (J, V-torsor K, section x of Σ*_J), i.e. M_{0,4} over the stack of Klein-four data
ideas.modern_name: M_{0,4} ≅ λ-line, relation with M_{1,1}[2] and Legendre family
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical; stack-theoretic versions in e.g. Deligne–Rapoport / later literature

deep.surprise_reason: A careful, base-independent (over arbitrary S, 2 invertible) torsor-theoretic description of the moduli of 4 points on P^1 via Klein-four quotient and the Fermat conic as universal Kummer cover. Elegant and characteristic of Grothendieck, but mathematically classical and consistent with known stack descriptions of M_{0,4} / M(2); nothing a specialist would find new.
